name: Dollar General
fiscalYearEnd: Friday closest to January 31 (fiscal 2025 ended January 30, 2026; the company's 'fiscal 2025' is TJX's 'fiscal 2026' year)

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Dollar General logo.svg, hosted on commons.wikimedia.org)

description: Dollar General is the largest US discount retailer by store count: 20,959 small-box stores in 48 states and Mexico (February 27, 2026), mostly in small towns, with about 75% of the US population within five miles of one. Nearly all money comes from selling everyday household basics at low prices (typically $10 or less), and 82% of FY2025 sales are consumables (food, paper and cleaning products, health and beauty, pet), which carry the lowest gross margin; the higher-margin seasonal, home and apparel goods are only 18%. It has one reportable segment; operating profit fell 30% in fiscal 2024 to $1.7B (including $214.2M of store-closure impairments) and recovered to $2.2B in fiscal 2025 as lower shrink (theft and damage) and higher markups lifted gross margin 107 basis points. Growth comes from new stores (about 450 planned in 2026), remodels (Project Renovate and Project Elevate) and a small Mexico rollout.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label as listed in Wikipedia's 'List of S&P 500 companies' (GICS Sector and GICS Sub-Industry columns, read 2026-09-30). No industry group or industry column in that source, so those are null. SEC SIC code is 5331 (Retail-Variety Stores), from the EDGAR submissions record.

hq.note: Executive offices in about 356,000 square feet of owned buildings in Goodlettsville, TN (FY2025 10-K, Item 2); incorporated in Tennessee

businessLines.name: Consumables
businessLines.how: Retail markup on staples people buy weekly; low margin per item, but drives the store visits and traffic that carry the other categories.
businessLines.description: Paper and cleaning products, packaged food, perishables (milk, eggs, bread, frozen food, beer, wine, produce), snacks, health and beauty, pet supplies and tobacco products. The largest category and, per the 10-K, the lowest gross-margin one.

businessLines.name: Seasonal
businessLines.how: Retail markup on discretionary goods, concentrated in the fourth-quarter Christmas selling season; among the highest gross-margin categories per the 10-K.
businessLines.description: Holiday items, toys, batteries, small electronics, greeting cards, stationery, prepaid phones and accessories, gardening, hardware, automotive and home office supplies.

businessLines.name: Home products
businessLines.how: Retail markup on household goods; among the highest gross-margin categories per the 10-K.
businessLines.description: Kitchen supplies, cookware, small appliances, light bulbs, storage containers, frames, candles, craft supplies, and kitchen, bed and bath soft goods.

businessLines.name: Apparel
businessLines.how: Retail markup on basic clothing sold at everyday low prices.
businessLines.description: Basic clothing for infants, toddlers, girls, boys, women and men, socks, underwear, disposable diapers, shoes and accessories.
